header: Date: 2026-12-27 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Lena Ortiz (Redwood), Jordan Lee (Moneta), Priya Raman (Moneta), Evan Brooks (Moneta)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Moneta through Optimize recommendations focused on batching and prefix/KV cache tradeoffs. Main topics: expected cost savings with KV cache for conversational flows, batching strategies to improve GPU utilization without breaching latency SLOs, quantization/throughput considerations, and plan for a benchmark run. Customer cares about 99th percentile latency < 250ms for chat, data residency and SOC2. Action items and timeline agreed.
topics: Prefix/KV cache sizing and eviction policy
Cost model: tokens saved vs additional memory/GPU overhead
transcript: 00:00:00 Speaker 1: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, we'll kick off the optimize walkthrough in a minute
00:00:07 Speaker 2: Hi all, Lena here, I'll take the deep dive sections on batching and kv-cache ops
00:00:12 Jordan Lee: Hey Samir, thanks. Quick note we got the calendar invite, we ran through the pre-read but excited to see the cost model in practice
00:00:20 Samir Patel: Great, agenda  quick context from Moneta, then we'll show batching patterns, prefix vs kv cache, cost math, and recommended next steps

00:00:32 Priya Raman: For context our primary workload is customer support chat and an insights assistant. Volume is about 3M user messages/month, median session length 6 messages, peak 120qps, 99p latency target 250ms

00:00:50 Lena Ortiz: Cool, that maps well to the sweet spot for prefix caching  you get repeated prefixes across sessions so the KV cache can cut down autoregressive tokens by ~30-60% depending on prompt reuse
00:01:05 Evan Brooks: What's the overhead of the KV cache memory-wise? We have limited GPU RAM and don't want to push into the need for extra nodes

00:01:12 Lena Ortiz: Good q  tradeoff is memory vs token compute. For a 13B-ish model with 16k context, storing KV for warm prefixes is typically a few GB per shard; we showed a few profiles in the doc. For Moneta's traffic our rough calc shows 8-12GB extra across the pool to capture high-frequency prefixes  saves around 25-40% token compute at peak in our sim
00:01:36 Jordan Lee: Sim? Is that based on our sample prompts? We uploaded a small set yesterday
00:01:41 Lena Ortiz: Yes we used the sample prompt set you shared and a synthetic session generator. It's approximate but directionally accurate  that's why the benchmark run is key

00:01:50 Samir Patel: Now batching  we typically suggest dynamic batching with latency-aware cutoffs. So for tail-sensitive workloads you set a max batching delay of 20-30ms and a max batch size tied to GPU topology
00:02:05 Jordan Lee: So dynamic batching won't blow our 99p? We can't have long added jitter

00:02:10 Lena Ortiz: Right, the idea is continuous batching: small delay window to collect requests, but prioritize requests close to SLO. In Redwood Optimize there's a policy engine that routes by latency buckets; high-priority traffic bypasses batching if it risks SLO breaches
00:02:27 Priya Raman: How do we model cost? Is it token-based in the sheet?

00:02:32 Samir Patel: We break it into two pieces: raw per-token GPU cost (inferred from throughput/seq-len) and amortized KV cache memory cost + extra capacity. The net is tokens_saved * token_cost - amortized_memory_cost. We put the math into the spreadsheet

00:02:45 Lena Ortiz: Example from our sim: with a 30% token reduction via KV caching and a modest memory overhead, net cost per 1M messages drops ~22% on our baseline. If you couple that with batching improvements at 1.8x throughput, effective unit cost drops more
00:03:05 Evan Brooks: Is that assuming you keep the same model/quantization? We might choose an int8 quantized model for cost
00:03:11 Lena Ortiz: Yes that was with a 4-bit quantized model profile. Quantization effects throughput and latency
00:03:27 Jordan Lee: Re: fallback  if cache misses spike, do you have graceful degradation to hosted fallback or smaller models?

00:03:33 Samir Patel: Absolutely, policy engine can route to a lower-cost model variant or a different capacity tier. For Dedicated we recommend a fallback to a smaller model under sudden load; for Hosted we use multi-model routing and region fallback
00:03:45 Priya Raman: Security question  if we store prefix KV that's derived from user messages, how is that encrypted and audited? SOC2 is required for us

00:03:53 Samir Patel: KV cache content is treated as ephemeral model-state, but in Private/Dedicated we can encrypt at rest with your KMS. Audit logs capture cache ops, and we can provide retention windows. We'll share the SOC2 and security whitepaper
00:04:08 Lena Ortiz: Also worth noting: we recommend hashing or normalizing PII before caching to reduce risk and memory footprint
00:04:15 Jordan Lee: Good call. Back to batching  any guidance on batch size per GPU? We run A100 80GB nodes

00:04:23 Lena Ortiz: With 80GB A100 you can push larger batches; for 13B-like models we typically see diminishing returns after batch 48-64 on a single GPU for latency-sensitive workloads. If you run multi-GPU shards, effective batch can be higher but you must watch cross-shard latency
00:04:40 Evan Brooks: Can Redwood Optimize automatically suggest these hyperparams? Or is it manual?

00:04:44 Samir Patel: There's an auto-suggest engine in the console  it looks at your traffic profile, LLM family, seq-length distribution and recommends batching delay, max batch size, cache TTLs. Lena will show a quick walk-through

00:04:56 Lena Ortiz: (screen share) here's the console snapshot  auto-suggest flagged that your median seq len is 180 tokens, so we suggest a small batching window and a KV cache TTL of 5 minutes for conversation starters
00:05:10 Jordan Lee: Can TTL be per-prompt? We have a few prompt templates that are reused more than others
00:05:15 Lena Ortiz: Yes you can set TTL at route level or per-prompt tag. Tag high-volume templates and keep long TTLs, keep ephemeral calls low TTL or disabled
00:05:26 Priya Raman: On eviction policy  LRU vs frequency  what's recommended?

00:05:31 Lena Ortiz: LRU is simplest; frequency-based (LFU) helps if a small set of prefixes dominate. For Moneta we saw a 12-item hot set where LFU gave slightly better hit rate. The console exposes both
00:05:43 Jordan Lee: Any pitfalls to watch for in rollout? We don't want a negative regression in quality or latency

00:05:50 Samir Patel: Start with a canary: enable KV caching for 5% of traffic and compare token counts, latency, and quality metrics. Redwood's eval hooks can compare outputs for a labeled prompt set  we'll help you set up regression alerts
00:06:05 Priya Raman: How do we measure quality drift introduced by batching or cache priming? We saw weird truncations before when trying aggressive batching in-house

00:06:13 Lena Ortiz: Quality issues often stem from batching-related prompt truncation or KV priming introducing context mismatch. We recommend tests at multiple batch sizes and include golden prompts in the eval set. The Optimize dashboard surfaces a quality delta alongside cost delta
00:06:28 Jordan Lee: For the benchmark run, what's the scope? We can give a small infra testbed but need Redwood SEs to run it

00:06:34 Samir Patel: Scope: run 4 workload patterns (steady low, steady high, spiky peak, long-conversation sessions). Metrics: tokens saved, throughput, 50/95/99 latencies, model output similarity scores, and memory footprints. We'll coordinate SE access to your testbed or use a staging VPC
00:06:50 Evan Brooks: If we do staging VPC, do you need network peering? We prefer to keep production isolated

00:06:56 Samir Patel: We can run within your VPC with a private deployment option; alternatively we can ingest sampled anonymized traffic into our sandbox for early sims. We'll do the former for full fidelity
00:07:08 Priya Raman: Timing  we want this pilot done before our Q1 budgeting review mid-Jan
00:07:12 Samir Patel: Ok we proposed dates in next_steps to start the benchmark week of Jan 10th. We'll get the scheduling invite after Samir sends the runbook
00:07:20 Jordan Lee: About cost model sensitivity  what's the biggest lever? Cache hit rate or batching efficacy?

00:07:25 Lena Ortiz: In most chat workloads cache hit rate is the highest leverage: 1% absolute increase in hit rate yields better token savings than small changes in batching. Batching helps reduce infra overhead and increases throughput, but hit rate compounds across session length
00:07:38 Evan Brooks: Do you have a rough ROI threshold? Like we need at least 15% cost savings to justify Dedicated additions

00:07:44 Samir Patel: We typically see customers justify Dedicated or reserved capacity if combined optimizations lower unit cost by >20% and improve tail latency. But that's a commercial convo  we'll include sensitivity buckets in the spreadsheet
00:07:58 Jordan Lee: Can you talk through an example math row in the sheet?

00:08:03 Lena Ortiz: Sure: baseline tokens per session 1400, cost per token $0.00012 => baseline $0.168 per session. With KV cache hit rate 35% you save 490 tokens => saved $0.0588. Memory amortized cost across sessions maybe $0.01/session => net saving $0.0488 (29% reduction). Then batching increases throughput reducing infra cost another 10% net
00:08:30 Priya Raman: Nice. Any gotchas with multi-tenant data? We sometimes share models across customers internally

00:08:36 Samir Patel: For multi-tenant, prefix collision and privacy are concerns. Recommended: tenant-tagged caches, per-tenant namespaces or scoped caches. Dedicated offers stronger isolation if you need it
00:08:48 Jordan Lee: We also use vector DB for retrieval  how does KV cache interact with retrieval-augmented flows?

00:08:54 Lena Ortiz: KV cache sits at the autoregressive state level, not the retrieval layer. For RAG, you can cache the prompt + selected docs prefix; if your retrieval is stable across sessions you'll get compounded savings. But you must watch freshness of retrieved docs
00:09:06 Evan Brooks: Does Redwood Optimize measure cache hit/eviction metrics in the console?
00:09:10 Lena Ortiz: Yes, dashboard has hit rate, per-route cache footprint, top N prefixes, and eviction churn. We also do synthetic cache warming pre-rollouts
00:09:20 Jordan Lee: About rollout policy  can we do a percent rollout by route?
00:09:24 Samir Patel: Yep, canary by percentage and by user segment. We recommend starting with internal traffic and then 5% external as mentioned
00:09:32 Priya Raman: Ok let's talk security docs  send SOC2, encryption playbook, and the KV cache data flow diagram
00:09:38 Samir Patel: Will do. I'll attach the security pack in the follow-up email
00:09:43 Jordan Lee: On cost: can your pricing model show Dedicated vs Hosted for our projected Q1 volumes? That would help our procurement
00:09:50 Samir Patel: Yes we'll provide two scenarios in the sheet: Hosted per-token pricing w/ optimize discounts and Dedicated reserved capacity amortized monthly. We'll call out break-even points
00:09:59 Lena Ortiz: Quick demonstration of the cost sheet (screen share): here are sensitivity sliders for hit rate, batch factor, and reserved commit  you can see cost curves shift live
00:10:12 Jordan Lee: That interactive sheet will be handy for our CFO
00:10:15 Evan Brooks: Any examples of customers with similar profile?
00:10:19 Samir Patel: Yes, we recently worked with SummitPay  similar chat workload  they saw ~24% net savings with combined KV + batching after a 6-week pilot. We'll send the anonymized case study
00:10:30 Priya Raman: Good  can you include that in the follow-up?
00:10:33 Samir Patel: Yep
00:10:35 Jordan Lee: A few micro-questions: 1) do we need model changes for prefix caching? 2) what's the expected cold-start behavior?

00:10:42 Lena Ortiz: 1) no model code changes required  it's runtime-level KV management. 2) cold-start: you get zero hit-rate initially; we recommend cache pre-warming with historical sessions or synthetic warmers. Cold-start period depends on traffic  could be hours to days
00:10:56 Priya Raman: For privacy we prefer synthetic warmers to avoid storing raw customer PII
00:11:00 Samir Patel: Makes sense  we'll include a template warmer script
00:11:05 Jordan Lee: Ok wrapping up, any final notes?
00:11:09 Lena Ortiz: We'll prepare the benchmark runbook and the cost sheet, and we'll set default TTLs and batching presets for your review
00:11:16 Samir Patel: Action items recap: Samir send playbook + pricing; Lena prep benchmark runbook; Priya provide prompts; schedule run week of Jan 10. Anything else?
00:11:27 Priya Raman: That covers it. Also please include the security pack
00:11:31 Samir Patel: Will do. Thanks everyone
00:11:34 Jordan Lee: Thanks Samir, Lena  talk soon
00:11:37 Speaker 2: Thanks all, meeting end
